The PT and PTT results are within normal ranges, so a coagulation factor deficiency like Hemophilia is unlikely. Since your platelets are normal and your clotting times are fine, does the bleeding occur spontaneously or only after minor injuries, and have you ever noticed large, painful bruises without any cause?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Von Willebrand Disease.

The normal platelet count, PT, PTT, and fibrinogen levels, combined with your history of easy bruising and post-extraction bleeding, strongly suggest a qualitative platelet defect or mild von Willebrand disease. We can confirm this with a vWF activity assay if needed, but based on the exclusion of other causes, this is the most likely diagnosis.
